name: The Newbury Boston
positioning: Restored landmark hotel in Boston's Back Bay, first opened in 1927 as the first Ritz-Carlton, at Newbury and Arlington Streets facing the Boston Public Garden
best_for: Travelers who want a Back Bay base facing the Boston Public Garden
Couples who want a wood-burning fireplace suite between October and April
Food lovers who want Major Food Group's rooftop Italian restaurant, Contessa, on site

facts.text: The hotel stands at the intersection of Newbury and Arlington Streets in Boston's Back Bay.
The Boston Public Garden is directly in front of the hotel.
The Boston Public Garden, America's first public botanical garden, is just steps from the hotel.
Before a two-year renovation and its reopening as The Newbury in May 2021, the property was the Taj Boston.
The guestrooms feature custom-designed furnishings by interior designer Alexandra Champalimaud.
The guestrooms feature original artwork by illustrator Veronica Lawlor.
Contessa was designed by Ken Fulk and serves Italian cuisine with sweeping city views.
Contessa is the first Boston venture by New York-based Major Food Group.
Afternoon Tea is served in The Street Bar, with fireplaces and views of Newbury Street, and the menu is curated by Major Food Group.
Rooms have Frette linens and robes and Byredo toiletries designed exclusively for the hotel.
The Mansion is a Presidential Suite with a wood-burning fireplace and 15th-floor views of the Boston Public Garden.

highlights.text: The building originally opened in 1927 as the first-ever Ritz-Carlton hotel.
Contessa is the hotel's glass-enclosed, four-season rooftop restaurant by Major Food Group.
From October 9 through April 10, a Fireplace Butler prepares and tends the fire in select suites.
The Library, connected to The Street Bar, offers literary reads curated by the Boston Public Library and is reserved exclusively for hotel guests.
Tiffany's Boston flagship is located in the hotel's lobby.

considerations.text: The hotel has no spa, though Newbury Street has many salon and massage options.
Arlington Street can be noisy, but suite bedrooms are set away from the street side.
WhataHotel notes the urban setting has limited parking availability.
